main_issue: Whether Agent D may wear her prayer-bead bracelet covered under her sleeve tomorrow, or whether it must be taken off entirely under the new no-visible-jewellery rule.

A-B.evidence: B asks if the rule includes D's bracelet and says she has to take it off (2, 4); B says it has to be off, not just hidden (16); A: 'Agent B's right' (17).

A-C.evidence: C says covering satisfies 'visible' (10, 12, 26); A says 'End of discussion' (27); C answers 'You're not head office' (28).

A-D.evidence: D offers to cover, then tape it, then says she cannot take it off for religious reasons (13, 15, 22); A insists it must be off, 'I'm sorry, but it has to come off' (23, 27).

B-C.evidence: B says it must be off, not just hidden (16); C counters 'That's not what the rule said' (19).

B-D.evidence: B says D has to take it off (4) and rejects her taping offer (16); D says she cannot take it off (13, 22).

C-D.evidence: C asks whether D can cover it (5), D agrees (6); C defends covering against A (10, 12, 21), and D offers to keep it covered (13).
